Paper/background is yellow/parchment-heavy. Faces are generic illustrated approximations and do not match Aachu/Zuv references. Style is anime/cartoon-adjacent and violates the hard reject list.

root_cause_summary: The active view_image queue used 1200x900 reference-binder contact sheets, not the raw high-resolution identity/style photos. Each identity photo was reduced to a 260x260 thumbnail inside a labeled sheet, weakening face-match signal.
The QA gate proved binder visibility but did not prove that the active generation path used high-fidelity identity inputs strongly enough to satisfy real face matching.

The prompt repeated warm/yellow-prone concepts such as warm lamplight, warm glow, warm ivory, paper grain, camel/tan, terracotta, and vintage palette. The negative 'no yellow' instruction was present but lost against stronger positive warm-scene/style cues.

The prompt over-combined identity, style, scene, typography, palette, brandmark, and negative constraints in one long request; imagegen optimized for an appealing generic watercolor scene and text accuracy instead of strict identity preservation.
Operator error: slide 1 already showed hard-reject failures, but generation continued to slide 2 instead of immediately blocking and recording Image QA rejection.
required_repair_before_retry: Use raw selected Aachu/Zuv face anchors as first-class visible image inputs, not only binder contact sheets, or mark IDENTITY_REFERENCE_INPUT_UNPROVEN.
Reduce warm/yellow language and require neutral white/off-white paper with no lamp wash bleeding into background.
Add a preflight output-quality gate that rejects yellow/anime/generic faces after the first candidate and prevents continuing the batch.
Separate identity-lock prompt from style/scene prompt or otherwise give identity references stronger generation priority.
